title: Bold text ending in punctuation is no longer recognised when followed directly by a letter (breaks Korean and similar text)
spec:
This is the Python-Markdown library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q`. Since the latest release, strong/emphasis that ends with punctuation is left as literal asterisks when a letter follows the closing delimiter without a space. This is very common in Korean, where particles attach directly to the preceding word. Input: `markdown.markdown('**단어(설명)**입니다.')` Expected: `

단어(설명)입니다.

` Actual: `

**단어(설명)**입니다.

` The same happens in English, e.g. `**Hello (world)**text` stays as literal `**`. Version 3.11.0 rendered both correctly. The new release appears to enforce CommonMark's punctuation rules for where emphasis may open and close (for instance `a**"foo"**` is no longer emphasised either). For backwards compatibility those punctuation rules should not be enforced: please restore the previous behaviour for emphasis next to punctuation, while keeping the rest of the emphasis handling as it is now.
acceptance: The reported Korean input renders as expected

Emphasis next to punctuation behaves as it did before the punctuation rules were introduced (e.g. `a**"foo"**` gives `

a"foo"

`); other emphasis behaviour is unchanged
A regression test is added and existing tests that assert the stricter punctuation behaviour are updated
